title: Staggered fintech adoption on loan default rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
To estimate the causal effect of fintech adoption on loan default rates, we'll use a Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach. The DID method is suitable for this scenario because we have a staggered treatment design where banks adopt fintech at different points in time. The key assumption is the parallel trends assumption, which states that the treatment and control groups would have followed parallel trends in the absence of the treatment. We use the `treated` variable to identify the treatment group and the `post` variable to identify the post-treatment period.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(plm)
library(broom)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s08_data.csv")

# Convert the data to a pdata.frame for panel data analysis
pdata <- pdata.frame(data, index = c("unit_id", "period"))

# Run the DID regression
did_model <- plm(y ~ treat_x_post, data = pdata, model = "within")

# Print the model summary
summary(did_model)

# Tidy the model output
tidy_output <- tidy(did_model)

# Print the coefficient of the treatment effect
print(paste("The treatment effect is: ", tidy_output$estimate[1]))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient of the `treat_x_post` variable to be negative and statistically significant, indicating that the adoption of fintech reduces loan default rates. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the specific characteristics of the data, but we expect it to be in the range of -0.05 to -0.10, suggesting a 5-10% reduction in loan default rates after fintech adoption. This is because algorithmic credit scoring is expected to improve the accuracy of credit assessments, leading to better loan decisions and reduced default rates.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Staggered DID (Callaway-Sant'Anna or Sun-Abraham) — cohort-specific ATTs; treatment=fintech adoption
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Fintech-adopting banks reduce default rates relative to non-adopters
